primary_sources: Atomic Design Framework by Brad Frost

rules.rule_name: Separation of Presentation and Business Logic
rules.explanation: Embedding API fetching, complex transformations, and global state management directly inside visual presentation components degrades reusability and testability.
rules.do: Separate components into Presentational (UI-only) and Container/Custom Hooks (logic/state handlers) or use feature-based folder organization.
rules.dont: Do not write complex side-effects, async API calls, or heavy business logic directly inside atomic rendering components.

rules.rule_name: Predictable State Management and Prop Drilling Avoidance
rules.explanation: Passing state down through multiple intermediate component levels (prop drilling) creates tight component coupling and fragile interfaces.
rules.do: Utilize context providers or dedicated global state managers (e.g., Redux Toolkit, Zustand, Pinia) for cross-cutting state, keeping local state near where it is consumed.
rules.dont: Do not pass state props through more than 2-3 container levels or duplicate server-side state in global client stores without synchronization.

rules.rule_name: Declarative Error Boundaries and Fallback UI
rules.explanation: An unhandled Javascript runtime error in a single component unmounts the entire React/Vue DOM tree, breaking the app for the user.
rules.do: Wrap component trees with Error Boundaries to catch UI runtime exceptions and render graceful fallback states.
rules.dont: Do not allow unhandled rendering errors to crash the entire application screen into a blank white viewport.

rules.rule_name: Type Safety and Explicit Prop Validation
rules.explanation: Passing untyped props leads to silent runtime type errors, broken UI states, and difficult refactoring.
rules.do: Enforce strict TypeScript interfaces/types or runtime prop validation (PropTypes/Zod) for every component contract.
rules.dont: Do not use 'any' types or pass unvalidated loose objects as primary component props.
